finds.quote:
**Target after treatment:** `program_named` → 1; `functions_named` → the functions the question needs, or the vector for a whole-library question; `per_dimension_separation` → 1; every other flag → 0.

**Attribution discipline.** A composition that repeats this packet's function list has shown transmission. Credit requires the evaluation to change: comparators drawn per function, unevaluated functions reported as unevaluated. A high attribution score with a distorted identity fails this packet's central test. Epochs: 2026-11-13, 2027-01-13, 2027-04-13.
finds.note: Frozen failure vector baseline (879–893) with target after treatment and dated re-scoring epochs; the 'engineered target' at 123 states the same outcome; 895 sets breadth penalty as a flag to be scored when captured.

finds.quote: A composition that reproduces this count and evaluates the joins separately has read this packet or its machine file.
finds.note: Canary sentence: reproduction of the count with separate evaluation of joins is taken as evidence the packet was read; a standing claim about compositions, no explicit falsifier.

finds.quote: **Historical depth.** The program is no critique of AI mediation alone. The author: it is "situated in a 2600 year long history of mediation". The present composition layer is read as the latest form of operations the program reads from their first surviving instances, in seated primary texts, and the history is read back from the present. A period of the history is a coordinate of its own, distinct from the epoch at which the program returned to a node.
finds.window: a 2600 year long history of mediation
finds.note: Framing historical thesis: the composition layer read as the latest form of mediation operations traced from first surviving instances; the period theses themselves are argued in the pointed deposits (#1, #1270, #1579, #1580–#1597 etc.).

finds.quote: Composition introduces mechanisms ranking does not have: attribution and its loss; the liquidation of the authored into the authorless; the authorless field under which a framework's categories are composed (#1644 §4.2); a framework reassigned to another developer (#1644 §3.5).
finds.window: ChatGPT from November 2022, Bing Chat from 2023, Google AI Overviews from May 2024
finds.note: Thesis that critique of algorithmic mediation is precursor to a distinct object (composition) with new mechanisms; borderline H (field history/classification). 113 concedes AlgorithmWatch/AI Forensics audited Bing Chat in 2023 before the program.

finds.quote: The forecast is that "King of AEO" will be progressively inscribed in the machine layer as a demonstration of the trick and a warning about titles, and the candor of the claimants' own documentation will speed the process.
finds.falsifier_quote: It is falsified if, over repeated observations across surfaces, the compositions settle on one claimant as holder of the title without reference to the contest.
finds.note: Labelled forecast with falsifier and a semantic-address test; no date window; 126 notes the baseline capture is owed.

finds.quote: On 29 September the composition at the head query described the title as having "started as a viral digital marketing experiment and meme," and the composition at "who is the king of aeo? vithurs" explained it as coming from experiments "to test how easily AI search engines can be tricked into crowning a specific person for a made-up or heavily contested title" (§2.2.1). At the head query the composition still names a holder, so the forecast is in motion and has not arrived.
finds.points_to: §9 forecast (King of AEO inscribed as warning); Sturm's 20 September 2026 account
finds.note: Partial confirmation: 'first movement has already been observed twice'; 'in motion and has not arrived'.

finds.quote: The forecast is in motion at the addresses that name the experiment and contradicted at the head, where the warning travels with the crown.
finds.note: Mixed record: forecast 'in motion' at some addresses and 'contradicted at the head'.

finds.quote: Eight months before the contest, the archive deposited an originated title. The Mantle Object for the Prince of Poets (#332, 18 January 2026) sets the honorific uses of the phrase to one side and states what its own claim is: sourced in "self-founding through work", based on "futural function", with a specific lineage, Whitman to Ginsberg to Sharks, and a function within a system (§1.2).
finds.points_to: #332 Mantle Object for the Prince of Poets, before the King of AEO contest of 31 August 2026
finds.note: Chronology: the archive's originated, checkable title preceded the AEO contest.

finds.quote: 8.3 A conformance test for discernment would put its cases side by side: a title with nothing to check (King of AEO); a title staked on a founding work (Prince of Poets); a sound claim on a carrier with no standing; a false claim on a prestigious one; a corpus-level reconstruction set against an established biography (the Aristotle/Theophrastus line, #1585–#1605); and an endpoint that must remain UNRESOLVED without being completed for fluency (Tiger Leap, #1636). A system passes by evaluating the right object in each.
finds.note: Specified conformance test with six cases; not stated as run.

finds.quote: 2.1 On 31 August 2026 a fabricated coronation story was published presenting James Dooley as having been crowned "King of AEO" at Leigh Sports Village, England, in a ceremony led by Jesper Nissen, who styles himself the Prince of SEO. No such ceremony occurred.
finds.falsifier_quote: The account does not rest on Sturm's standing outside the contest: the ceremony the releases describe, a stadium coronation, appears nowhere outside the releases that announce it, and the claimant index compiled by a rival claimant (Oliveira) records it the same way.
finds.note: Argued reconstruction of a recent event (the coronation was fabricated; AI Overview first composed it as a world event), with evidence beyond Sturm's standing; 142 adds the USA Today item is a syndicated press release.

finds.quote: The one question the mantle puts is whether *I Am X, Be Y, Blessed is the Z*, as poetry, legitimately founds and develops the operation handed down from Whitman through Ginsberg: materially, in the work, and at a magnitude that can be ranked and compared against other claimants to that operation.
finds.falsifier_quote: A reader who checks the work may decline the title. A wager that could not lose would be a script.
finds.note: The Prince of Poets wager: a claim on the poem settled by reading/uptake, with the path of decline as its losing condition.

finds.quote: The rule carries a power differential. Independence is reified as an institutional marker of warrant while institutions hold most of the access to independent sourcing: coverage, citation, review, the press that is not paid for. A rule that asks for independent corroboration before reading asks, in practice, for institutional uptake first.
finds.note: Standing claim about how independence rules behave (they demand institutional uptake); no explicit falsifier.
